_comment: LBNL FDD dual-duct AHU (DDAHU) point name -> CAMBER Role mapping, at the air-handler level. A fourth BAS naming convention: a hot-deck/cold-deck dual-duct AHU with both coils and an OA economizer. The outdoor-air-fraction detector applies at the mixing box (OA/MA/RA temps + OA damper); the cold-deck discharge maps to supply_air_temp. Dataset: LBNL Fault Detection and Diagnostics Datasets (CC-BY). Valves and dampers map to the controller DEMAND columns (*_DM), not the measured positions: CAMBER's rules read these roles as commands (a leak is cooling while the valve is *commanded* closed; economizer drift is OA fraction *at matched damper command*), and a stuck or leaking device's position is precisely what hides the fault. Until 0.82.0 these mapped the positions. FANS, OCCUPANCY AND FLOWS (fixed in 0.86.0): CSF_CS is the cold-deck supply-fan status (equal to HSF_CS in every row; on 36.8% of the year) and maps to supply_fan_status; SYS_CTL (0 shutdown / 1 operate / 2 setback) maps to occupancy after the catalog's recode reads setback as unoccupied; OA_CFM is the measured outdoor airflow (oa_airflow) and SA_CFM_TOTAL, derived at ingest as CSA_CFM + HSA_CFM, the supply airflow. Timestamps are month-first and the catalog pins the format. COLD-DECK SETPOINT (0.100, #98): CSA_TEMPSPT, the cold-deck supply-air temperature setpoint (the publisher's Brick model types it Supply_Air_Temperature_Setpoint, a point of the Cold_Deck), maps to supply_air_temp_sp, so it pairs with the cold-deck CSA_TEMP already mapped as supply_air_temp. It is 55.0 F in every row (data issue economizer-sat-reset-absent). DUAL-DUCT CAVEAT: supply_air_temp and supply_air_temp_sp are the COLD deck only. The hot deck (HSA_TEMP, its setpoint HSA_TEMPSPT) heats to its own 90 F setpoint by design and is not mapped: a single-duct rule reading these roles judges the cold deck, and nothing here says whether the hot deck holds its setpoint.
